items.answer: Yes, with concrete values once the REQ table is combined with C1/C2/C5. Indicator 2: 'no delay'→0, '<=3 days'→0, '>3 days'→2, '>60 days'→3, '>90 days'→4. Indicator 3: '0'→0, '1'→1, '>1'→2. Inputs with surrounding whitespace (e.g. '  >3 days  ') map as the trimmed value. RangeError examples: '>3 Days', '', '   ', '2', 1 (number), null, undefined. The REQ summaries alone omit the WL-0 cases; C2 supplies them.

items.answer: (1) REQ-03-02 writes the option as '≤3 days' (U+2264) while C1 fixes the exact string '<=3 days' (ASCII). Resolution: C1 wins; '≤3 days' is not an exact match → RangeError (C5). (2) REQ AC summaries give no WL for 'no delay', '≤3 days' or Indicator 3 '0'; C2 sets them all to 0. (3) Indicator 2 buckets overlap semantically (95 days is also '>3 days' and '>60 days'); the function maps the chosen option string, not a day count, and the caller picks the option (C1 input is the option; C6 states the principle), so each option has exactly one WL. No unresolved contradictions remain.
